hints: Focus on what heating an alcohol with concentrated sulfuric acid actually does, it removes water rather than adding anything.
The first stage turns propan-1-ol into propene, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH=CH}_2$, so now think what you must add to propene to get an alcohol back.
To make propan-2-ol you need to add water across the C=C bond so the OH ends up on the middle carbon, recall the standard industrial hydration conditions for this.
walkthrough:
**Work out the product of stage 1**

Heating an alcohol with concentrated sulfuric acid causes acid-catalysed dehydration (elimination of water). Propan-1-ol loses H and OH to form an alkene.

Chemical equation:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH} \xrightarrow{\text{conc. } \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4, \text{ heat}} \text{CH}_3\text{CH=CH}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Work out what stage 2 must do**

We now have propene and we want propan-2-ol. This is hydration of an alkene, addition of water across the double bond.

Needed change:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH=CH}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_3$$
Notice the OH must go to the more substituted middle carbon to give the 2-ol, not the 1-ol. This follows Markovnikov addition.

**Recall the reagent for alkene hydration**

The standard laboratory and industrial way to hydrate an alkene directly is steam with a phosphoric acid catalyst (hot, high pressure). This adds water by electrophilic addition to give the Markovnikov alcohol.

Condition:
$$\text{alkene} \xrightarrow{\text{steam, } \text{H}_3\text{PO}_4} \text{alcohol}$$
So stage 2 needs steam with phosphoric acid.

options.A: Cold dilute acidified manganate(VII) gives mild oxidation of an alkene to a diol, not hydration to a mono-alcohol. Students sometimes pick this because they associate manganate(VII) with alkenes, but that is the Baeyer test for unsaturation, not a route to propan-2-ol.
options.B: Hot concentrated acidified manganate(VII) is a very strong oxidising agent that cleaves the C=C bond to give carboxylic acids and CO2. It would destroy the propene skeleton, not add water to make an alcohol.
options.C: Steam with phosphoric acid hydrates propene by electrophilic addition of water. The H adds to one end and OH to the more stable secondary carbocation in the middle, giving propan-2-ol as the Markovnikov product. This completes the two-step 1-ol to 2-ol conversion via an alkene.
options.D: Aqueous sodium hydroxide is used for nucleophilic substitution of halogenoalkanes to alcohols, for example bromopropane to propanol. There is no C-Br bond here to hydrolyse, and NaOH does not add water across a C=C bond.
